experiments.why: A catalogued tile whose instance has a description must still be captioned with the tile's name.
A catalogued tile whose name holds %s, with no engraving, now goes through engravedName instead of showing the tile's name.
An engraving containing $$ checks that filling the %s does not treat it as a replacement pattern.
A tile gone from the catalogue used to fall back to the description and now skips it for the tile id.
A tile gone from the catalogue with an inscription, which only the new code reads as the fallback.
A castable stone whose instance has a description but no inscription, which the new code stops using for the button name.
A placement with no item id must give null even when it carries an inscription.
A placement with an inscription and an engraving, which the new instance carries over.
Empty inscription and engraving must be left out of the instance, not written as keys.
A natural weapon name with surrounding spaces, which the new save writes trimmed.
A blank weapon name must be left out of the save rather than written as an empty key.
Interactions with nothing enabled must save as undefined.
A battler's immunities with padding and a blank entry, which the old save dropped entirely.
A battler's remains tile id with spaces, which only the new save writes, trimmed.
A wall is not an item, so the card must be null.

source.quote: is empty for a body carrying no stones

obligations.statement: castableStones returns [] for a body carrying no stones (only a sword).

source.quote: has one button per stone, in square order

obligations.statement: castableStones returns one button per castable stone the body carries, ordered by square.

source.quote: leaves out a stone the caster has not earned

obligations.statement: castableStones leaves out a stone whose mastery requirement the caster does not meet (an adept-stone with arcane 9 gives []).

source.quote: offers it as soon as the mastery is met

obligations.statement: castableStones includes a stone as soon as the caster's mastery meets its requirement (an adept-stone with arcane 10 gives one button for adept-stone).

source.quote: leaves it out while the caster is part-way through another cast

obligations.statement: While the caster is part-way through a cast, castableStones still leaves out an unearned stone and keeps the earned one (only the weapon square remains).

source.quote: carries the stone's own sprite and its cooldown

obligations.statement: A castableStones button carries the stone's own tileId and sprite and the cooldown left on that stone.

source.quote: reads the same across one second of cooling

obligations.statement: castableStones gives the same reading for a stone with 4400 ms and with 4001 ms of cooldown left, apart from the instance id.

source.quote: Automatic stones are absent entirely

obligations.statement: castableStones leaves automatic (passive) stones out of its result entirely instead of returning them as dimmed buttons.

obligations.authorized_by: Two name fallbacks follow the inscription rather than the description, because it was the inscription doing that job all along: a sign in your bag is called what it says rather than "Sign", and so is a stone in the cast bar.

source.quote: The name comes off the instance's description before the tile's

obligations.statement: castableStones names a stone's button with the instance's description when it has one, and with the tile's name only otherwise.
obligations.why: the pull request says it changes this

source.quote: The tile's name rather than the instance's description

obligations.statement: slotCaptionFor captions an instance whose tile is in tilesById with that tile's name, even when the instance carries its own description.

source.quote: Committed on close, not per keystroke.

obligations.statement: PlacementSettingsDialog commits its text fields to the placement when the dialog closes, whether by Done, the close button or Escape, and not on each keystroke.

source.quote: Null for anything that is not an item, which is most of what a player can

obligations.statement: itemCard returns null for a tile that is not an item, such as a wall.

source.quote: one-second cadence pay out exactly N times

obligations.statement: Over the life of an N-second status with a one-second cadence, advanceStatuses fires its effect exactly N times, not N-1.

source.quote: a status whose cadence is shorter than the catch-up owes every one

obligations.statement: When one advanceStatuses call's tickMs spans several cadence periods of a status, the effect fires once for every period owed, not only once.

source.quote: adds to what is left and clamps at the authored ceiling.

obligations.statement: Re-applying a stacking status adds the rolled duration to its remaining time, capped at the status definition's ceiling.

source.quote: refreshes to the longer of the two, never the newer.

obligations.statement: Re-applying a non-stacking status sets its remaining time to the longer of the current remainder and the new roll, so it never shortens.

source.quote: One draw either way, taken before the branch

obligations.statement: applyStatus takes exactly one draw from rng per call, whether it adds a new status or extends one already present.

source.quote: The latest cause wins on a re-application

obligations.statement: When a status already present is applied again with a causedBy, applyStatus records the new cause in place of the earlier one, for stacking and non-stacking statuses alike.
obligations.why: the quote is in a comment of app/game/statuses.ts that is not applyStatus's own and does not name it

source.quote: An absent cause on a re-application therefore clears one that was there,

obligations.statement: Re-applying a status without causedBy clears the cause previously recorded on it.
obligations.why: the quote is in a comment of app/game/statuses.ts that is not applyStatus's own and does not name it

source.quote: `maxMs` is a property of the condition, not of the meal.

obligations.statement: When applyStatus is given a duration range by what hands the status over, the remaining time is still capped at the status definition's own maxMs.
obligations.why: the quote is in a comment of app/game/statuses.ts that is not applyStatus's own and does not name it

source.quote: Replaced wholesale rather than mutated

obligations.statement: applyStatus returns a new list and leaves the list passed in unchanged.

source.quote: Persist interactions; omit the field entirely when nothing is enabled.

obligations.statement: interactionsForSave returns undefined when no interaction is enabled, so the field is left out of the save.

source.quote: Null rather than minting one on the spot

obligations.statement: instanceFromPlacement returns null for a placement that carries no item id, and never invents one.

source.quote: Optional fields are omitted rather than set to `undefined`

obligations.statement: The instance returned by instanceFromPlacement has no keys set to undefined: optional fields the placement lacks are left out.
